term: innocence in the hard case and Aquinas’s innocent/righteous contrast
resolution: Aquinas contrasts innocent and righteous people with sinners in his common-good argument, without defining a general test for innocence. The formal hard case stipulates innocence and nonthreat separately for one victim. These senses are compared without an identity or implication; applying the historical argument to this precise case requires an additional interpretive and factual bridge.
